task: Two direct, independent questions in one message: '1. i want option to set background color as transparent. 2. is it possible to have multiple assets within a single experience?' Investigated both directly in the code before answering. Item 1 turned out to have two real, stacked gaps, both fixed: (a) the Colour Experience's Scene-hosted 'Transparent' checkbox was a documented no-op -- checking it never actually cleared/transparentized the background at all -- fixed by having it genuinely force the background fill Layer's opacity to 0 (or, unchecked, honour the existing colorOpacity slider), reusing setSceneBackground's own established 'an ordinary full-bleed fill Scene Layer, not a special field' mechanism, matching Engine Invariant 8 ('Canvas has no background property... a special scene.background field would be exactly the second way to do something Elements-in-Layers already do'); (b) even with a genuinely-transparent background Layer authored, both rendering engines (Builder's engineRuntime.js and Studio's renderer/slideRenderer.js) painted an UNCONDITIONAL opaque backdrop fill before any Layer ever drew, so the transparency could never actually show through -- fixed by adding a matching _hasExplicitBottomFill/_hasSlideFullBleedFill check to each engine, skipping that fallback fill ONLY when a Theme Author has explicitly authored a full-bleed background Layer, so the Layer's own (possibly fully transparent) opacity becomes the real, honest result. Deliberately kept the fallback's own default behaviour completely unchanged for every Scene/theme with no such Layer authored -- a zero-regression, purely additive/opt-in design, not a sweeping change to what every existing theme shows by default. Matches Creator Governing Rule #1 (Fidelity) and #5 (Publish Fidelity): Builder's own preview and Studio's real render now agree on transparency exactly as they must. Item 2 answered directly rather than built: confirmed via direct code reading (_ensureExperienceDefaults's own doc comment) that 'Only-one-content-type-at-a-time' is a deliberate, already-shipped product simplification from Builder V3.1 -- an Experience's contentKind restricts rendering to exactly one of Text/Image/Graphics/Colour, a real product decision, not a bug or a gap -- so no new capability was built for this; the real workaround (multiple separate Experiences placed together in one Scene) and an offer to build either 'combine kinds' or 'multiple images in one slot' as a genuine follow-up were communicated directly instead. Verified via a new 8-assertion Playwright suite spanning all three affected surfaces: World Builder's own EngineV2Runtime.render() directly (no-fill-layer fallback unchanged; opacity-0 genuinely transparent; opacity-1 paints the real colour with no cream bleed-through); real ProjectModel/UI-flow calls simulating the Colour Experience's Transparent checkbox (unchecked honours colorOpacity; checking forces opacity to genuinely 0, not a silent no-op; unchecking restores colorOpacity); and Studio's renderer/slideRenderer.js render(s) directly with a synthetic compiled theme (no full-bleed fill Layer -> opaque fallback fully unchanged; a full-bleed fill Layer at alpha 0 -> genuinely transparent, not the opaque fallback). Full regression across the existing render-pipeline-touching Playwright suite (stretch fit, text alignment fidelity, text newline fix, image rotation, text rotation, text rotation pivot, rotation-honoured-through-real-Publish-export, and a real Museum Gallery .vtheme byte-for-byte pixel-hash/Museum-Caption-drag-and-resize regression) all pass completely unchanged, plus both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js, tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js, and renderer/slideRenderer.js.
